title: Operate EMT worker and retained installation state
summary: Understand EMT configuration, readiness, worker admission, schedule intent, explicit maintenance and matched installation instructions.
use_when: EMT configuration, worker admission, readiness, installation instructions or explicit maintenance behavior must be understood.
do_not_use_when: The goal is a product-domain intervention result or Nucleus execution authority itself.
outcome: Understand EMT configuration, readiness, worker admission, schedule intent, explicit maintenance and matched installation instructions.
effects: Configuration, admission, scheduling, maintenance, installation and activation are separate effects. Worker activation can read accounts, start authorized agent work and submit mail. Installation before initialization only installs bytes.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/EMT/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.

Direct install remains limited to uninitialized EMT state. It rejects an enabled worker binding and runs the disable transition for a retained disabled binding to wait for active processes before runtime publication.
authority: EMT owns private configuration, incident and exchange state, admission, holds, matched publication. Clockwork owns scheduling and failure halts; Nucleus owns jobs; Email owns credentials and transport.
success: Verify matched program/provider, valid configuration, known drain counts and the selected schedule, pause, hold and exact halt intent. Doctor observations do not prove receiving access or delivery.
failure_and_recovery: Installation failure leaves completed effects in place. Interruption requires inspection before an explicit next operation; no automatic replay, rollback or recovery occurs. Explicit maintenance releases only its exact owned hold. Preserve unknown counts and existing halts; initialized direct selector recovery is unsupported.
privacy: Correspondence, Nucleus references and quota records remain private and retained without automatic deletion. EMT stores no credentials; other providers retain separate copies. Ordinary status and logs omit bodies.
does_not_authorize: Unrequested activation, account reads, mail, another owner's hold release, implicit failure-halt approval or direct initialized selector recovery.

consumers.statement: The current user, authorized EMT worker and operator of installation instructions or explicit maintenance.

preconditions.statement: Initialization and maintenance require current-user state access, selected compatible dependencies and authority for the chosen operation.
New assignments require valid configured receiving domain and paths, Nucleus invocation policy two with workspace-unrestricted, and the prompt preparation prerequisites owned by emt.incident.respond.

inputs.statement: Configuration accepts the receiving domain, absolute stable Cell root, agent cwd, model and provider executable paths. Maintenance identifies the exact hold owner; migration requires drained work.

outputs.statement: Doctor returns bounded local and dependency observations with receiving permission and final delivery not_probed. Status reports retained counts. Maintenance status reports protocol_version, holds, drained and outstanding exchanges; migration returns the current schema version and initializes paused state when absent.

data_semantics.statement: Configuration, operator pause, schedule enablement, maintenance holds and failure halts are separate states. Status counts are retained records, not lifetime totals or product-health verdicts. Unknown maintenance counts are not zero.

identity_and_units.statement: emt/worker is the Clockwork binding. Holds belong to exact owners. Worker interval is 15 seconds and activation timeout is 300 seconds; schema-one domain state and release identities have separate meaning.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Doctor describes local schema, SQLite quick_check, Clockwork interface, Nucleus health and Email executable presence at probe time. It sends no mail and submits no job. Maintenance drain advances existing exchanges without discovering new incidents or replies.
No timer-latency, service-availability, maximum recovery duration, future support lifetime or retention-horizon objective is promised.

access.statement: Supported current-user CLI and matched installer operations govern private state under ~/Library/Application Support/EMT. Explicit exchange reads can expose correspondence; live activation requires separate account, investigation and email authority.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Init creates paused schema-one state. Configuration changes require paused and drained work. Pause stops new discovery while admitted exchanges continue; resume validates configuration and routes Clockwork EMT notifications without enabling a schedule or approving a failure halt.

The worker skips overlap and does not wait for model completion. The declared deploy instruction publishes bytes, initializes or migrates local state, saves configuration, configures the Clockwork route and publishes intended worker selection under ordinary admission and runner locks. It creates no maintenance hold, drains no exchanges and performs no health, content or signature audit. Existing pause and failure-halt intent are preserved unless explicitly selected settings change operator intent.

Explicit emt migrate checks drained schema-one state or initializes absent paused state. It copies no database or configuration. Deployment retains no migration-completion receipt and performs no automatic recovery; initialized direct selector recovery remains unsupported.

operational_limits.statement: Worker scheduling is every 15 seconds without run-at-load, with a 300-second activation timeout and overlap skipping. Ordinary Nucleus or Email unavailability is waiting; unexpected local or Clockwork interface failure ends the current pass. Clockwork permits later activations before the shared service-health threshold. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Healthy or inactive checks clear a pending episode. An established halt requires exact approval.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Only EMT schema one is accepted. The matched cell-install-v4 release includes binary, installer and Chancery bundle. Old pinned Clockwork brokers must be replaced before routing or running with claims.
No future support lifetime or retention horizon is promised.

reliances.statement: Clockwork owns the worker schedule, incident feed, notification checks, routing claims and failure-halt continuation.
Nucleus owns job readiness, execution and maintenance; requester-only updates leave Nucleus admission open.
Email owns receiving-account settings and credentials; deployment resolves the receiving domain through its supported interface.
Quota deferral and frozen shared-notice progress keep their independent admission and delivery rules.
